html:
The Guahibo, who call themselves Sikuani or Hiwi, are an Indigenous people of the Llanos, the grassland plains of the Orinoco basin in eastern Colombia and western Venezuela, along the Meta, Vichada and Tomo rivers. They are one of the largest Indigenous peoples of the Llanos.

Traditionally they moved in bands through the savanna and the forests along its rivers, hunting, fishing and gathering, and some groups farmed. Jesuit missions on the Orinoco and Meta tried to settle them in the 1700s. As cattle ranchers spread across the plains in the 1800s and 1900s, some went on "guahibiadas", hunts in which Guahibo people were killed; a 1967 massacre at the La Rubiera ranch became a national scandal in Colombia. Their neighbours include the Achagua, the Pumé and the Puinave.
